sources.notes: Personally read NPS GrandTeton relative-elevation article: abundant coarse sediment, varying discharge, exposed midchannel bars and interweaving multithread channels. Personally inspected actual NPS/Potter fall photograph, not just LiDAR visualization: broad exposed tapered gravel bars divide blue shallow flow into unequal joining arms; bars and banks are irregular and asymmetric.

sources.rights_note: Original generated concept used as design guidance only; not a primary factual source or texture.
sources.notes: Long-axis Y flow; branch network repeatedly splits and rejoins around three offset bar groups and a cross-connecting arm. Water surface kept below continuous bank terrain and unequal exposed bar crests; terrain is carved by distance to the same branch-network centerlines. Bar forms arise in network voids rather than separate discs placed on a water sheet. Closed terrain cutaway with natural low relief and a few embedded faceted gravel stones. No vegetation required for bare sediment reference scope. Concept inspected: connectivity useful, but concept has overly repeated symmetric almond bars. Correct final branch network to unequal asymmetric widths, staggered junctions and differently shaped bars, not copy those ovals.
